sections.h2: Putnam County recorder: address, phone and hours
sections.html:
The Putnam County Recorder works from 245 E. Main Street in Ottawa, the same street address the county auditor uses. The phone is 419.523.6490, the toll-free line is 888.638.0042 and the fax is 419.523.4403.

The office opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, while the recording window shuts at 4:15. It is closed on the usual holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas and the November holiday for military service.

sections.h2: The order of stops for a deed
sections.html:
Three stops come before the recorder sees a deed, and the order matters, because an unstamped deed is turned away.

  1. Take the legal description to the Tax Map Office, which sits in the engineer's office and answers at 419-523-6931. All legal descriptions must be pre-approved, and the document must meet the county's conveyance standards.
  2. Once the tax map staff sign the document, bring it to the auditor, who transfers it and collects the conveyance fee.
  3. Record the transferred deed with the recorder, who follows the standards and fees on its own site.

The auditor is at 245 East Main Street in Ottawa, 419-523-6686, on a weekday 8:30 to 4:30 schedule. Under Tools on the auditor's site sits a calculator that prices the transfer before you go.

The auditor charges four dollars for each thousand of price, with the price rounded up to the next hundred, and fifty cents a parcel in transfer fee. The conveyance is not processed unless the check matches the conveyance fee to the penny.

Form DTE 100 accompanies a normal sale, and DTE 100 (EX) is the version for deeds that claim an exemption. The county's forms page carries both, so you can fill them in ahead of the visit.

A separate county transfer tax is possible under R.C. 322.02, capped at 30 cents on each $100 and owed by the grantor. Ask the auditor whether Putnam County has one in force. The calculator gives the quickest total.

The recorder charges $4.00 for each marginal notation. The base amounts come from R.C. 317.32.

  • Pages one and two: $34 together, half base fee and half housing trust fund.
  • Later pages: $8 each, split the same way.
  • A preservation surcharge, capped at $5 an instrument, goes to the county's general fund.
  • A certified copy costs $2 a page in total.

A document that fails the county's standards costs $20 more. Those rules, under R.C. 317.114, call for 10-point type or larger, dark blue or black ink, no highlighter, and letter or legal paper. Page one needs three inches clear at the top, later pages an inch and a half, and the sides and bottom an inch. Exempt are court papers, plats, DD 214 discharges, state and federal documents, and anything signed before July 1, 2009.

Three offices handle the paperwork on a sale.

The auditor's home page also posts a delinquent real estate list and counts 29,689 parcels as of 2023. If your house may have fallen behind on taxes, check that list.

A short checklist saves a second trip.

  • Get the legal description pre-approved at the Tax Map Office, 419-523-6931.
  • Fill in DTE 100, or DTE 100 (EX) if the deed claims an exemption, from the county's forms page.
  • Price the transfer on the auditor's calculator and write one check that matches the conveyance fee to the penny.
  • Bring a separate check payable to the Putnam County Recorder for recording, and arrive before the 4:15 recording cutoff.
  • Check the format rules so the $20 nonconforming charge does not apply.

If a mortgage was paid off, the release needs a full legal description too, so a parcel number alone will not do. A title company can handle all of this for you if you would rather not make the trip.

E-recording now covers deeds and other transfer documents, through three approved vendors: Simplifile at 1.800.460.5657, CSC at 1.866.652.0111 and Erecording Partners at 1.888.325.3365. You work through one of them rather than the county directly.

Documents recorded at the counter go back immediately, documents e-recorded are returned immediately, and documents delivered by mail are sent out the next business day. The office requires a full legal description, including on releases and assignments, so a mortgage satisfaction needs more than a parcel number.

At the counter, checks are made payable to the Putnam County Recorder. If you mail a paper, allow for the next-business-day return and for the time the auditor's transfer takes first.

The records search is online and the indexes are open to everyone. Viewing images needs a free online subscriber form, and documents are indexed on the computer starting January 1, 1993. A recording notification service is also offered.

The Tools menu holds sales reports and delinquency reports, the conveyance calculator and a tax estimator. A GIS parcel viewer sits behind the Map link, and an Info section holds the forms the state and the office provide.

The 2025 delinquent parcels list is posted there too. Search your parcel before listing, and phone the auditor if the record looks off.

sections.h2: Century Farms and other recorder services
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the office runs the county's Ohio Century Farm registrations. A farm qualifies after 100 years in one family, and qualified registrants receive an heirloom certificate signed by the Governor and the Director of the Ohio Department of Agriculture. A yard sign is available for purchase. The recorder will meet with you to check eligibility, so ask before you sell a farm that might qualify. The office also keeps military discharge records, the DD 214 files.

Putnam County is mostly rural, with 34,451 people over 484 square miles. Owners occupy 83.8% of occupied homes, and there are 13,824 housing units, 6.1% of them vacant.

sections.h2: Selling a farm, an estate home or a house with a balance
sections.html: These sales follow the same paperwork. The legal description goes to the Tax Map Office, the auditor transfers the deed, and the recorder files it. A cash buyer can purchase the property in its present condition and cover these fees at the closing table, which spares you the repairs and the wait for a lender. Cash Home Buyers CA can explain how the fees are handled at closing.

faqs.q: What are the Putnam County recorder's hours?
faqs.a: Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, with recording accepted from 8:30 to 4:15. The office closes on the holidays listed on its contact page.

faqs.q: What does the auditor charge for a deed transfer?
faqs.a: Four dollars per thousand of price, rounded up to the next hundred, plus fifty cents a parcel. The check has to equal the conveyance fee exactly.

faqs.q: Do I need approval before bringing a deed to the recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Map Office in the engineer's office must clear the legal description, and the auditor must transfer the deed before it reaches the recorder.

faqs.q: Does Putnam County accept e-recorded deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. E-recording covers deeds and transfer documents, through the vendors the recorder lists: Simplifile, CSC and Erecording Partners.

faqs.q: How much is a marginal notation?
faqs.a: $4.00 for each one. A nonconforming document costs $20.00 more.
